used.how: the copies must be in place before the layer: plans for the NEXT chunk, copies carried by other layers' calls, a fence call, a host guard that runs a layer off when its copies are not fenced
fill budget MOE_FILL_PIECES=125 pieces a source port a call and MOE_FILL_CAP=4 reused as the planner's per-port budget and the job pages' cap word; link 0 of the first hop
no same-chunk planner: the plan comes from the previous call's counts, exchanged on the device after the layer (no count exchange inside the head)
the deliverable is measured on the real novel / code prompts back to back (tests/test_moe_prev_replicas.py), not on the A/B's random-token profile
the planner reads head.counts as one row-major uint32 page of chips x spc words ([1, 1, 1, slots])
no stock whole-mesh all_gather for the counts: the planner program's own sender cores send each chip's counts over the fabric (tail_send's pattern)
the planner's 0.21 ms counts wait in the host-bound 4-layer quick model read as launch skew, confirmed in the full model (15 us)
every pass is a fresh request from chunk 0 (new state), with an off-vs-off repeat that must be bit-identical as the baseline check
bit-identity of prev vs off relies on COMBINE_SPLIT's order-free combine sums (the default); checked per chunk (max |diff| 0)

missing: Blackhole (this Galaxy compiles -mcpu=tt-bh) DRAM NoC alignment for small writes into a page: the planner writes whole 1 KB job pages (read-modify-write) to stay 64 B aligned; no entry says what a 32 B write at a 32 B offset does
the head's counts hold only a chip's own slots: a cross-chip consumer needs its own exchange (written in tt/expert_prev.py)

overseer.evidence: nothing padded or duplicated to fit a kernel: the landing rows are 16-word DRAM pages (alignment), the copies are only the planner's chosen replicas; fork extended (per-job weight addresses) instead

the planner and reset programs are Python-built (MeshProgramDescriptor) and dispatched through ttnn.bringup.prepare_program / run_prepared, built once, 8 + 3 x senders addresses patched a call (asserted: patch_count); host time per call measured in the gate unit: planner dispatch 92.5 us median, pre-call guard + fill args 4.9 us (~3.9 ms a chunk); the reset program runs once a request
no fork regression suite run; only the model test test_moe_prev_replicas.py and the measure parts
